---

## Enabling the filter

```yaml
filters:
  - toc-depth
```

## The attribute

```markdown
## Section {toc-depth=1}
```

| Attribute | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `toc-depth` | non-negative integer | How many levels below this heading appear in the contents. `0` removes the heading itself. |

: The attribute accepted on any heading. {.striped .hover tbl-colwidths="[18,22,60]"}

The depth is relative to the heading that carries it.
`toc-depth=2` on a level-two heading lists that heading and its level-three children, and stops there, whatever level the heading sits at.

| Value | Effect on the heading | Effect on its subtree |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `0` | Removed from the contents, and unnumbered. | Removed and unnumbered, all the way down. |
| `1` | Listed. | Not listed. |
| `2` | Listed. | Direct children listed; anything deeper is not. |
| `n` | Listed. | Listed down to `n` levels below it. |

: What each value does. {.striped .hover tbl-colwidths="[10,40,50]"}

## The document default

```yaml
extensions:
  toc-depth:
    default: 1
```

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | non-negative integer | | Applied to every heading with no explicit `toc-depth`. |

: Document and project options. {.striped .hover tbl-colwidths="[15,22,12,51]"}

An attribute on a heading always beats the document default.

## The cascade

A heading's depth applies to everything beneath it, until a descendant sets its own.

A descendant with an explicit `toc-depth` takes over the cascade for itself and its own subtree, and can widen it or narrow it.

```markdown
# Parent {toc-depth=1}

## Child A

## Child B {toc-depth=3}

### Grandchild B1
```

`Child A` is hidden, inherited from `Parent`.
`Child B` overrides with a wider depth, so `Grandchild B1` is listed even though its parent's parent asked for one level.

The same works in the other direction: `toc-depth=0` on one child hides that subtree while its siblings stay visible under a wider parent.

## Quarto's own `toc-depth`

Quarto has a document option of the same name, and it is applied first.

```yaml
toc-depth: 3
```

That option decides how deep the contents can go at all; this extension then removes entries within it.
The two compose in one direction only: a heading attribute can narrow what Quarto would have listed, and cannot widen it beyond Quarto's own limit.

::: {.callout-caution}
`toc-depth=3` on a level two heading asks for its level five descendants, and Quarto's default of `3` has already excluded everything below level three.
Raise the document option when a heading attribute asks for more than it allows.
:::

## Validation

| Rule | On failure |
| --- | --- |
| The value is an integer. | Warns, and the heading falls back to the document default, or to normal Quarto behaviour. |
| The value is not negative. | Warns, and the value is clamped to `0`. |

: Validation rules. {.striped .hover tbl-colwidths="[40,60]"}

## Format support

The filter sets Pandoc's `unlisted` and `unnumbered` classes on headings, which is the mechanism Quarto uses itself.

| Format | Contents | Numbering |
| --- | --- | --- |
| HTML, RevealJS | Yes | Yes |
| LaTeX, PDF | Yes | Yes |
| Typst | Yes | Yes |
| Word | Depends on the template | Yes |
| Markdown, PowerPoint | No contents to affect | |

: What each format does with the classes. {.striped .hover tbl-colwidths="[28,36,36]"}

## Limitations

- The extension controls what the contents list, not how it is laid out.
- `toc-depth=0` also unnumbers the heading. The two go together in Pandoc's model and cannot be separated here.
- Word honours the numbering; whether the contents follow depends on the template in use.
